_meta.federal: CFPB's Jan 2025 rule banning medical debt from credit reports was vacated by a federal court (Cornerstone Credit Union League v. CFPB, E.D. Tex., July 11, 2025); it never took effect. In Oct 2025 the CFPB issued a non-binding interpretive rule claiming the FCRA preempts state credit-reporting laws; courts have not settled this. Equifax, Experian and TransUnion still voluntarily exclude paid medical debt, medical collections under $500, and medical debt less than 1 year past due. The federal No Surprises Act (2022) bans most surprise bills for emergency care and out-of-network providers at in-network facilities (not ground ambulances). Nonprofit hospitals must have financial assistance policies and wait 120 days before most 'extraordinary collection actions' (IRS 501(r)).
_meta.caveats: General information, not legal advice; laws change often and many have income limits, exceptions, or apply only to certain providers (e.g. hospitals, nonprofit hospitals). Credit-reporting bans in 16 jurisdictions are verified against NCLC (Sept 2026), but state bans face preemption challenges: Colorado's is being litigated (ACA Int'l v. Fulford, no ruling as of Sept 2026) and a Texas law was held partly preempted (CDIA v. Paxton, Aug 2026). 'surprise' entries apply only to state-regulated (fully insured, non-ERISA) plans and are summarized from pre-2026 trackers; ground-ambulance coverage lists are partial (about 22-24 states have some protection). 'charity' and 'collections' entries for states not covered by 2025-2026 trackers rely on older law and should be spot-checked before launch. null means no notable state rule found, not a guarantee none exists.

Arizona.interest: Interest on medical debt capped at 3% (Prop 209, 2022)
Arizona.surprise: State arbitration for surprise out-of-network bills of $1,000+ in state-regulated plans
Arizona.collections: Wage garnishment capped at 10% and home equity up to $400K protected for consumer debts (Prop 209)

California.credit: Medical debt can't appear on credit reports (since Jan 2025)
California.interest: Payment plans for patients eligible for hospital discounts must be interest-free
California.charity: Free or discounted care for uninsured or high-cost patients under 400% of poverty at all hospitals
California.surprise: Bans surprise bills from out-of-network doctors at in-network facilities; ground ambulance too (2024 law)
California.collections: No hospital collections for 180 days; hospitals can't garnish wages or lien a primary home for most patients

Colorado.credit: Medical debt can't appear on credit reports (since Aug 2023); law is being challenged in court
Colorado.interest: Interest capped at 3%; none for patients eligible for financial assistance
Colorado.charity: Discounts under 250% of poverty; hospital bills capped at 4% of monthly income for eligible patients
Colorado.surprise: Bans surprise out-of-network bills in state-regulated plans, including ground ambulance
Colorado.collections: Hospitals must screen uninsured patients for aid before collections; waiting period before collection actions

Connecticut.credit: Medical debt can't be reported to credit bureaus (since July 2024)
Connecticut.interest: Interest on hospital bills capped at 5%
Connecticut.charity: Uninsured patients under 250% of poverty can't be charged more than the hospital's cost
Connecticut.surprise: Bans surprise out-of-network bills in state-regulated plans (emergency and in-network facilities)
Connecticut.collections: Hospitals must screen uninsured patients for aid before sending bills to collections

Delaware.credit: Medical debt can't appear on credit reports (since Oct 2025)
Delaware.interest: No interest or late fees allowed on medical debt (2025)
Delaware.surprise: Limits surprise emergency bills in state-regulated plans; ground ambulance protections

Florida.surprise: Bans surprise ER and out-of-network bills at in-network hospitals for state-regulated HMO/PPO plans
Florida.collections: No hospital lawsuits or harsh collections until 30+ days after itemized bill and aid decision; 3-year limit to sue (2024)

Georgia.surprise: Bans surprise ER and out-of-network bills at in-network facilities in state-regulated plans (2021)

Idaho.collections: No collections until 60+ days after final itemized statement; limits on fees and costs (Patient Act, 2020)

Illinois.credit: Credit bureaus can't report medical debt (since Jan 2025)
Illinois.charity: Uninsured patients under 600% of poverty get hospital discounts; yearly collections capped at 20% of income
Illinois.surprise: Bans surprise out-of-network bills in state-regulated plans; ground ambulance cost-sharing capped (2025)
Illinois.collections: Hospitals must screen uninsured patients for aid and offer payment plans before suing

Indiana.collections: Hospitals must tell patients about financial assistance before collections begin (2026 law)

Louisiana.interest: Interest on medical debt for necessary care capped at 3% (2026 law)
Louisiana.surprise: Ground ambulance balance-billing protections in state-regulated plans

Maine.credit: Medical debt can't appear on credit reports (full ban since Sept 2025)
Maine.interest: Debt collectors can't charge interest on medical debt
Maine.charity: Free hospital care under 200% of poverty (2025)
Maine.surprise: Bans surprise out-of-network bills in state-regulated plans, including ground ambulance
Maine.collections: No home liens or wage garnishment for medical debt (2026); payment plans capped at 4% of income under 400% poverty

Maryland.credit: Medical debt can't appear on credit reports (since Oct 2025)
Maryland.interest: Hospitals can't charge interest to patients eligible for free or reduced-cost care
Maryland.charity: Free hospital care under 200% of poverty; reduced-cost care above that
Maryland.surprise: Bans surprise bills for HMO members; ground ambulance protections in state-regulated plans
Maryland.collections: No hospital suits under $500; 240 days to apply for aid before collections; no liens on primary home

Massachusetts.charity: Health Safety Net pays hospital bills for residents under 300% of poverty (full under 150%)
Massachusetts.collections: Providers can't bill Health Safety Net-eligible patients for covered care beyond limited deductibles

Michigan.surprise: Bans surprise ER and out-of-network bills at in-network facilities in state-regulated plans (2021)

Minnesota.credit: Medical debt can't appear on credit reports (since Oct 2024)
Minnesota.charity: Hospital-AG agreements limit charges to uninsured patients with income under about $125K
Minnesota.collections: Can't deny needed care over unpaid bills; spouses not liable for medical debt (Debt Fairness Act, 2024)

Nevada.credit: Limited: hospitals not following price-transparency rules can't report medical debt (2025)
Nevada.interest: No interest or fees during required 60-day notice before medical debt collection
Nevada.charity: Larger hospitals must discount uninsured patients' bills by at least 30%
Nevada.surprise: Bans surprise ER bills in state-regulated plans (2019)
Nevada.collections: Collectors must send a 60-day notice before collecting medical debt (2021)

New Hampshire.surprise: Bans surprise out-of-network bills in state-regulated plans; ground ambulance too (since Jan 2026)

New Jersey.credit: Medical debt under $500 can't be reported to credit bureaus (since July 2024)
New Jersey.interest: Interest on medical debt capped at 3% a year (2024)
New Jersey.charity: Free hospital care under 200% of poverty, discounts to 300%; uninsured to 500% capped near Medicare rates
New Jersey.surprise: Bans surprise out-of-network bills in state-regulated plans (2018)
New Jersey.collections: Waiting period and limits on collection actions and lawsuits (Louisa Carmen Act, 2024)

New Mexico.credit: Low-income patients' (under 200% poverty) medical debt can't be reported or sold
New Mexico.surprise: Bans surprise out-of-network bills in state-regulated plans (2019)
New Mexico.collections: No lawsuits or collections against patients under 200% of poverty; must screen for aid (2021)

New York.credit: Medical debt can't appear on credit reports (since Dec 2023)
New York.interest: Interest on medical debt judgments capped at 2%
New York.charity: Free hospital care under 200% of poverty; sliding-scale discounts to 400% at all hospitals
New York.surprise: Bans surprise out-of-network bills; state arbitration process; ground ambulance protections
New York.collections: Hospitals and providers can't lien a primary home or garnish wages for medical debt; 3-year limit to sue

North Carolina.charity: Most hospitals joined a voluntary state program (2024) to relieve old debt and expand free care

North Dakota.interest: Medical debt interest limited (reported as 1% or $25 per month); verify
North Dakota.surprise: Ground ambulance charges limited to 250% of Medicare in state-regulated plans (2025)

Ohio.surprise: Bans surprise ER and out-of-network bills at in-network facilities in state-regulated plans (2022)

Oregon.credit: Medical debt can't appear on credit reports (since Jan 2026)
Oregon.charity: Nonprofit hospitals: free care under 200% of poverty, discounts to 400%
Oregon.surprise: Bans surprise out-of-network bills in state-regulated plans; ground ambulance protections (2025)
Oregon.collections: Nonprofit hospitals must screen patients for financial assistance before collections

Rhode Island.credit: Medical debt can't appear on credit reports (since July 2025; bureau ban added Jan 2026)
Rhode Island.interest: Interest capped at 1-year Treasury rate (1.5%-4%) on medical debt incurred after June 2025
Rhode Island.charity: Free hospital care under 200% of poverty; discounts to 300%
Rhode Island.collections: No liens/executions on homes or wage garnishment for medical debt (since Jan 2026)

Texas.credit: Limited: providers must meet billing conditions (e.g. cost estimate) before reporting; partly preempted (2026 ruling)
Texas.surprise: Bans surprise out-of-network bills in state-regulated plans; ground ambulance protections through Sept 2027

Utah.surprise: Ground ambulance balance-billing protections in state-regulated plans (2025)

Vermont.credit: Medical debt can't appear on credit reports (since July 2025)
Vermont.charity: 2025 law sets required hospital discount levels for lower-income patients
Vermont.surprise: Ground ambulance balance-billing protections in state-regulated plans

Virginia.credit: Providers can't report medical debt to credit bureaus (since Apr 2024)
Virginia.interest: No interest/late fees until 90 days past due, then capped at 3% (from July 2026)
Virginia.surprise: Bans surprise out-of-network bills in state-regulated plans; some job-based plans opt in (2021)
Virginia.collections: From July 2026: no home foreclosures for medical debt; wage garnishment limited; big hospitals restricted

Washington.credit: Medical debt can't appear on credit reports (since July 2025)
Washington.charity: Free care under 300% of poverty at large hospital systems (200% at others); discounts to 400%
Washington.surprise: Bans surprise out-of-network bills in state-regulated plans; some job-based plans opt in
Washington.collections: Hospitals must screen for charity care before collections

District of Columbia.credit: Medical debt can't be reported to credit bureaus (since Aug 2026)
District of Columbia.interest: Interest on medical debt capped at 3% a year (2026)
District of Columbia.charity: Free care under 200% of poverty; reduced-cost care to 500% (2026)
District of Columbia.collections: No collections for 180 days; no liens on primary home; no garnishment under 500% of poverty (2026)
